teams.heading: Ben Youngs criticises RFU chiefs for backing Steve Borthwick after review
teams.body: Former scrum-half Ben Youngs has criticised RFU bosses for showing 'blinkers' by backing head coach Steve Borthwick after a thorough review of England's worst-ever Six Nations campaign. Chief executive Bill Sweeney and performance director Conor O'Shea have publicly thrown their support behind Borthwick, reportedly offering a contract extension beyond the 2027 World Cup. With only three wins from eight Tests in 2026 — including a historic defeat against Italy — Youngs warned that the administrators must also be held accountable if this gamble fails in Australia.

lead.why: It highlights the major public debate and direct criticism from a former international regarding the RFU's long-term backing of Steve Borthwick.

teams.heading: IRFU dismisses World Rugby's proposal to move Six Nations matches to USA
teams.body: The Irish Rugby Football Union has clarified there are "currently no plans or discussions" regarding the relocation of Six Nations fixtures to the United States. The statement follows World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin suggesting that an Ireland v Italy clash in Boston or New York would resonate with expatriate fanbases. While acknowledging the US as an important growth market, the IRFU stressed that the competition holds a "special place" for home supporters and prioritised maintaining the tournament’s traditional appeal for fans in Dublin and Rome.

lead.why: It is the most significant strategic story, involving a direct response from the IRFU to World Rugby regarding the future of the Six Nations.

teams.heading: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada continues serving his two-Test match ban
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada remains suspended from all match-day proceedings, including stadium attendance, for the upcoming fixture against South Africa. The head coach was handed the two-Test ban by World Rugby for comments made regarding the match official following the meeting with the All Blacks. This sanction was the first applied under the governing body's new Match Official Abuse Sanctioning Process, which aims to reduce public criticism of referees and maintain confidence in officiating standards.

lead.why: The coach's ongoing suspension remains the most significant administrative development affecting the squad.

teams.heading: Ruthless Canada outclass Scotland in heavy WXV series opening defeat
teams.body: Scotland faced a difficult start to their WXV campaign on Saturday, falling 26-64 to a clinical Canada side at Hive Stadium. Despite a spirited effort featuring tries from Evie Gallagher, Shona Campbell, Lana Skeldon, and Rhona Lloyd, the visitors’ ten-try haul proved insurmountable. Interim head coach Dave Butcher’s squad struggled to contain the World Cup finalists’ relentless attacking rhythm throughout the 80 minutes. The hosts now face a quick turnaround as they prepare for next weekend’s fixture against New Zealand.

lead.why: The opening WXV fixture resulted in a significant defeat against a top-tier opponent, making it the most impactful news for fans today.

teams.heading: BBC Wales secures free-to-air coverage for the WXV Global Series
teams.body: Wales fans will have extensive access to the upcoming WXV Global Series following the announcement that matches will be broadcast live on BBC One Wales and BBC iPlayer. The series sees Wales host South Africa in Cardiff followed by a match against the USA. Tomos Grace, Chief Commercial Officer at the WRU, described the partnership as a vital step in reaching wider audiences, noting the women’s game remains the fastest growing part of the sport in the nation.

teams.heading: James Slipper pauses playing career to join Brumbies coaching staff
teams.body: Wallabies centurion James Slipper has been appointed as the Brumbies’ scrum coach on a temporary basis for the upcoming Super Rugby AUS campaign. The record-breaking prop, who recently signed a one-year contract extension, will move into the backroom staff to assist head coach Stephen Larkham while regular coach John Ulugia transitions to the national setup. Slipper stated, “I’ve been around a lot of scrums over the years, so hopefully I can pass on a bit of what I’ve learnt.”

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One grants equal status to naturalised long-term players
teams.body: Japanese rugby officials have officially rolled back controversial eligibility restrictions for the 2026-2027 season. Following recent pressure from naturalised athletes urging fairness, League One has confirmed that long-term naturalised players will now be afforded equal status within the competition. This decision marks a significant shift from earlier proposals that would have limited the participation of foreign-born players. The policy change aims to resolve the ongoing nationality dispute before the new domestic season begins in December.

teams.body: Coach Dave Rennie has reshuffled his side for the series finale in Baltimore, installing Richie Mo’unga at fly-half in a bid to ignite the tourists' attacking game. teams.heading: Springboks and All Blacks reach Baltimore for final rivalry series test
teams.body: South Africa arrives in the United States holding a 2-1 series lead, facing New Zealand at the M&T Bank Stadium in a fixture that serves as a pivotal staging post for the 2031 World Cup. While the Springboks look to secure the series, the match represents a significant commercial push for both nations. Rassie Erasmus, who reaches his 100th Test in charge, has made two changes to his squad, with Damian Willemse returning at full-back following Cheslin Kolbe’s jaw injury.
